summary: Modern databases and data platforms are increasingly embedding AI/ML capabilities directly into their engines, allowing developers to run inference, generate embeddings, and perform semantic vector search without exporting data to external systems. Capabilities range from native vector indexes and in-database LLM functions (e.g., Snowflake Cortex, BigQuery ML) to extension-based approaches (e.g., pgvector on PostgreSQL and Aurora). This keeps data in place, reduces governance risk, and simplifies building RAG and GenAI applications.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Cortex AI (LLM functions, Cortex Search, embeddings)
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex provides serverless access to hosted LLMs and embedding models via SQL/Python functions (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, EMBED_TEXT), plus Cortex Search for hybrid semantic retrieval. Data stays within Snowflake with no AI infrastructure to manage, and Cortex is now also extending to Snowflake Postgres.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a VECTOR data type with vector similarity functions (VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY, etc.) and Cortex Search provides managed semantic/vector search built into the platform.
databases.llm_integration: Native hosted LLMs (Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic, and others) exposed through Cortex SQL/Python functions and Cortex Agents.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based pricing in Snowflake credits, billed per token/compute for Cortex LLM and embedding functions on top of standard warehouse/storage costs.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets you create, train, and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time series, etc.) using SQL, and integrates with Vertex AI for generative models, remote model inference (ML.GENERATE_TEXT), and embedding generation (ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING).
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery supports a VECTOR_SEARCH function and vector indexes for approximate nearest neighbor search directly in SQL.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Vertex AI foundation models (Gemini, PaLM, text-embedding models) via remote models and generative SQL functions.
databases.pricing_notes: Charged under BigQuery compute/analysis pricing (on-demand per TB or capacity slots) plus Vertex AI model usage charges for generative and embedding calls.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector for embeddings and pgai for in-database AI workflows
databases.description: PostgreSQL gains AI capabilities through extensions: pgvector adds a vector data type with similarity operators and indexing, while pgai (and pgai Vectorizer) helps generate embeddings and call LLMs/embedding providers from within SQL, enabling RAG directly in Postgres.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to core PostgreSQL. Vector search is provided by the pgvector extension (HNSW and IVFFlat indexes); core Postgres has no built-in vector type.
databases.llm_integration: Via the pgai extension, which can call external LLM and embedding providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Ollama, and others) from SQL; not built into core Postgres.
databases.pricing_notes: PostgreSQL and both extensions are open source and free; costs depend on self-hosting/managed-service infrastructure plus any external model API usage.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you invoke ML models hosted in Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock (including LLMs) directly from SQL queries, passing row data to models for inference such as predictions, classification, or text generation without moving data out of the database.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native. Vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL is provided only through the third-party pgvector extension, not as a built-in Aurora ML feature.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker-hosted models invoked via SQL functions (aws_ml / aws_bedrock).
databases.pricing_notes: Standard Aurora instance, I/O, and storage pricing, plus separate charges for the underlying SageMaker endpoints or Bedrock model invocations.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML (in-warehouse ML with SageMaker & Bedrock)
databases.description: Redshift ML enables analysts to create, train, and deploy ML models using SQL CREATE MODEL statements, leveraging Amazon SageMaker Autopilot behind the scenes, and to invoke remote models including Bedrock LLMs for generative and embedding tasks directly in the data warehouse.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native as a first-class feature historically; Redshift ML focuses on model training/inference. Vector similarity must be handled via distance calculations or external services rather than a dedicated built-in vector index.
databases.llm_integration: Supports remote inference against Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker endpoints invoked through SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Billed under Redshift compute (RPU/node) and storage pricing, plus SageMaker training/inference and Bedrock usage costs.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model serving, training, agents) and Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks provides end-to-end AI through Mosaic AI for model training, fine-tuning, serving, and agent frameworks, combined with a managed Vector Search service that automatically syncs and indexes embeddings from Delta tables for RAG applications on the Lakehouse.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in, fully managed vector database with automatic index synchronization from source tables.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Model Serving and Foundation Model APIs provide access to hosted and external LLMs (Meta Llama, DBRX, Anthropic, OpenAI via external models) for inference, embeddings, and agents.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs) for compute, model serving, and vector search endpoints, on top of cloud infrastructure costs.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search lets you store embeddings alongside operational JSON documents and run approximate nearest neighbor semantic search using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage, enabling RAG and semantic retrieval combined with standard Atlas queries and filters.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Atlas Vector Search is a built-in capability using HNSW-based indexes and the $vectorSearch operator within the Atlas platform.
databases.llm_integration: No in-database LLM hosting; integrates with external providers (OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Hugging Face, LangChain, LlamaIndex) to generate embeddings and power RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Included within Atlas cluster pricing; vector search runs on Atlas Search nodes, so costs scale with cluster/node tier and storage.
